args.rationale: The patient has MRSA bacteremia with infective endocarditis. His circulation failed quickly and he went into cardiogenic shock. Echo showed a new area of the left ventricle not moving properly and fluid around the heart that progressed to tamponade. Drainage produced yellowish, cloudy fluid, and after drainage, coronary angiography showed the prior stent had broken down and a coronary pseudoaneurysm was rapidly enlarging. This fits an infected stent with an infected pseudoaneurysm and probable infected pericardial fluid. Pericardial drainage is only a temporary bridge. He needs emergency surgery to remove the infected tissue and stent, restore blood flow with bypass grafting, and wash out the pericardium.
args.followup_or_handoff: Hand off to cardiothoracic surgery, cardiac anesthesia and the cardiology/cath lab team to go straight to the operating room. Get blood crossmatched and prepared for major bleeding. Consider mechanical circulatory support (IABP/ECMO) if shock does not respond to treatment. Keep the heart well filled and use inotropes or vasopressors as needed. Send pericardial fluid and tissue taken during surgery for Gram stain, culture, susceptibilities, cell count and chemistry. Repeat blood cultures. No antibiotic order was recorded in this encounter. Ask infectious diseases to urgently review and continue MRSA-active IV antibiotics, such as weight-based vancomycin (goal AUC 400-600) or high-dose daptomycin 8-10 mg/kg IV daily, with doses adjusted to kidney function. Do a transesophageal echo during surgery to check for valve vegetations or an abscess. After surgery, he goes to the cardiac ICU.
